on.places: Shillong, Cherrapunji (Sohra), Nongriat, Mawlynnong, Dawki and the Umngot river, Laitlum Canyons, with Kaziranga from November
on.activities: The clearest weather of the year: canyon and waterfall views, the root bridge trek on drier paths, boating on the clear Umngot and, from November, Kaziranga safaris. Nights in Shillong turn cold from November to February, so carry warm layers. Rain can linger into early October.

mid.places: Shillong, Cherrapunji, Mawlynnong and Dawki; Kaziranga safaris usually run until about April
mid.activities: Warmer and greener, with pre-monsoon showers and afternoon thunderstorms that grow more frequent through May. Sightseeing and village walks work best in the mornings, waterfalls begin to fill, and prices are lower than in winter. Carry rain gear.

off.places: Shillong and the Cherrapunji viewpoints in clear spells; Kaziranga is usually closed
off.activities: The monsoon, with extremely heavy rain at Cherrapunji and nearby Mawsynram, among the wettest places on Earth. Waterfalls are at their most spectacular, but landslides, road delays, slippery root bridge trails and muddy Umngot water are common, and some boating and treks may be suspended. Keep the itinerary flexible and allow buffer days.

profile.overview:
Meghalaya, the Abode of Clouds, is a compact hill state in India's north-east where misty plateaus, deep gorges, caves and waterfalls sit close together. Within a few days you can stand at the edge of Laitlum Canyons in the morning, walk to a living root bridge grown by Khasi villagers from the roots of rubber fig trees, and watch boats drift over the glass-clear Umngot river at Dawki. Shillong, the capital, is a cool hill town with lakes, cafes and a lively music scene.

The state is easy to reach for Indian travellers: fly to Guwahati, then drive about three hours to Shillong. There is no visa to arrange and the roads between the main sights are good, though the hills make for winding drives. The best months are October to March; the monsoon from June to September is extremely wet. Tell us your dates, group size and comfort level, and we will build the route around you, with Kaziranga as an optional add-on.

facts.languages: Khasi, Garo and English (official); Hindi is widely understood in towns
facts.climate: Cool and pleasant at about 1,500 m, roughly 4 to 25 degrees C through the year, with very heavy monsoon rain from June to September
facts.flight_time: Fly to Guwahati: about 3 hr from Chennai and 2 hr 30 min from Delhi, then about 3 hr by road to Shillong. Guwahati is also well served by train.

reasons.title: Living root bridges and waterfalls
reasons.text: Khasi villagers have trained tree roots into bridges that are centuries old, and the Cherrapunji plateau drops away in some of India's tallest waterfalls.

reasons.title: A river as clear as glass
reasons.text: The Umngot at Dawki is so transparent in the dry months that boats seem to float on air, with the Bangladesh border a short way downstream.

reasons.title: Cool weather and no visa
reasons.text: Shillong and the plateau stay mild even when plains cities are hot, and Indian travellers need only a valid photo ID.

reasons.title: Easy to combine
reasons.text: Shillong, Cherrapunji and Dawki fit comfortably into five to seven nights by road from Guwahati, with Kaziranga as an extension.

reasons.title: Village life and homestays
reasons.text: Stay in or near Khasi villages such as Mawlynnong, where gardens, bamboo structures and a strong community culture are part of the visit.

attractions.title: Shillong city
attractions.text: Ward's Lake, the Police Bazaar and the Iewduh market, with colonial-era churches and cafes that earned it the name Scotland of the East.

attractions.title: Elephant Falls and Shillong Peak
attractions.text: A three-tiered waterfall in a forested gorge, and a viewpoint at one of the highest points in the Shillong area.

attractions.title: Laitlum Canyons
attractions.text: A ridge near Shillong that looks down over layered green canyons, best in clear morning light.

attractions.title: Nohkalikai Falls
attractions.text: One of India's tallest plunge waterfalls, seen from a viewpoint above Cherrapunji and at its fullest during and after the rains.

attractions.title: Mawsmai Cave and Seven Sisters Falls
attractions.text: A lit limestone cave you can walk through, and a seven-stream waterfall that spreads across a cliff face near Sohra.

attractions.title: Double-decker living root bridge, Nongriat
attractions.text: Two bridges grown one above the other, reached by a long stepped trek down from Tyrna village.

attractions.title: Dawki and the Umngot river
attractions.text: A border town on a river so clear that boats cast shadows on the riverbed, with boat rides and a suspension bridge.

attractions.title: Mawlynnong
attractions.text: A tidy Khasi village with bamboo dustbins, flower gardens and a short walk to a living root bridge nearby.

experiences.title: Trek to the living root bridges
experiences.text: Walk the stone steps to Nongriat and cross the double-decker bridge; allow most of a day and wear shoes with grip.

experiences.title: Boat ride on the Umngot
experiences.text: A calm ride on one of India's clearest rivers, best between November and March when the water is transparent.

experiences.title: Cave and waterfall day around Sohra
experiences.text: Mawsmai Cave, Nohkalikai Falls and Seven Sisters Falls make an easy, rewarding day from Cherrapunji.

experiences.title: Morning at Laitlum
experiences.text: An early start for soft light over the canyons, with tea and a walk along the ridge.

experiences.title: Homestay evening in a Khasi village
experiences.text: Simple stays in places such as Mawlynnong give you time with local families and village walks.

experiences.title: Kaziranga jeep safari (optional add-on)
experiences.text: A two-night extension to Assam for the one-horned rhinoceros, elephants and birds, usually open from about November to April.

food.title: Jadoh and Dohneiiong
food.text: Khasi rice-and-pork dishes, the best-known local meals. Both are non-vegetarian and rich, and widely served.

food.title: Tungrymbai and local vegetable dishes
food.text: Fermented soybean, strongly flavoured and eaten with rice; ask for a mild vegetable plate if you prefer.

food.title: Pukhlein and rice cakes
food.text: Sweet rice-flour snacks sold at markets and roadside stalls, good with strong tea.

food.title: Shillong cafes and bakeries
food.text: The city has a lively cafe scene, good coffee and bakeries, along with North Indian and Chinese restaurants.

food.title: Vegetarian and Jain meals
food.text: Easy in Shillong, simpler in Cherrapunji and the villages. Tell us in advance so we can arrange meals in the remote stretches.

tips.title: Plan around the monsoon
tips.text: June to September brings extremely heavy rain, landslides and slow roads. October to March is the comfortable season.

tips.title: Wear shoes with grip
tips.text: Root bridge trails and viewpoints are stepped and slippery when wet. Trekking sandals or sports shoes work best.

tips.title: Carry cash
tips.text: Mobile networks, ATMs and UPI can be unreliable in Cherrapunji, Dawki and the villages, so carry enough cash.

tips.title: Allow time for hill roads
tips.text: Distances look short but roads wind and can be slowed by traffic or rain, so we keep each day's programme modest.

tips.title: Layer up in winter
tips.text: Shillong nights from November to February are cold. Carry a light jacket and a warmer layer.

tips.title: Respect village customs
tips.text: Ask before photographing people, keep villages clean and follow your driver-guide's advice, especially near the border at Dawki.

travel_info.visa: Indian citizens need no visa for Meghalaya. Carry a valid government photo ID such as an Aadhaar card, passport, voter ID or driving licence, as hotels and some sites ask for it. We arrange any permits that apply and confirm the current rules at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations. Shillong is at about 1,500 m, so altitude is mild, but the trails to the root bridges are steep and tiring. Carry personal medicines, insect repellent and a rain jacket, and drink bottled or boiled water. Leeches are common on forest paths in the monsoon.
travel_info.money: ATMs are easy to find in Guwahati and Shillong but scarce around Cherrapunji, Dawki and the villages, and card or UPI payments may not work there. Carry enough cash for local meals, entry points and tips. Tipping your driver-guide is customary but optional.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Meghalaya?
faqs.a: Five to six nights cover Shillong, Cherrapunji, Mawlynnong and Dawki comfortably by road from Guwahati. Add the Nongriat root bridge trek or a Kaziranga extension for seven nights or more.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: October to March is the best season, with clear views and a clear Umngot river. April and May are warmer with showers, and June to September is the heavy monsoon, when roads, trails and boating can be disrupted.

faqs.q: How do I reach Meghalaya from Chennai?
faqs.a: Fly to Guwahati, about three hours, then travel by road to Shillong, about three hours. A few flights serve Shillong's Umroi airport, but Guwahati has the widest choice.

faqs.q: Is the root bridge trek difficult?
faqs.a: The Nongriat trek has thousands of steps down and back up, so it needs reasonable fitness and good knees. If you prefer an easier option, the root bridge near Mawlynnong is a short walk.

faqs.q: Is Meghalaya suitable for vegetarians and Jain travellers?
faqs.a: Yes, in Shillong and the larger towns. In Cherrapunji, Dawki and the villages the choice is simpler, so we arrange vegetarian and Jain meals ahead of time.

group_trips.title: Meghalaya Root Bridges, Waterfalls and Dawki Group Trip
group_trips.summary: Seven days through Shillong, Cherrapunji, Nongriat, Mawlynnong and Dawki, with the double-decker root bridge trek, Nohkalikai Falls and a boat ride on the Umngot, travelling in a small group.
group_trips.overview:
This group trip covers the best of Meghalaya over six nights, three in Shillong, two in Cherrapunji and one near Dawki. You see Shillong's lakes and waterfalls, stand above Laitlum Canyons, visit Mawsmai Cave, Nohkalikai Falls and Seven Sisters Falls, and trek down to the double-decker living root bridge at Nongriat.

The journey then moves towards the Bangladesh border, with a walk in Mawlynnong village and a boat ride on the clear Umngot river at Dawki. A trip captain travels with the group, and vegetarian and Jain meal options are available on request.

The Nongriat trek is steep and takes most of a day, so this trip suits travellers with reasonable fitness. The drives are on winding hill roads, and we keep each day's programme modest.

itinerary.description:
After breakfast, visit Elephant Falls, a three-tiered waterfall in a forested gorge.

itinerary.title: Laitlum Canyons | Drive to Cherrapunji
itinerary.description:

Visit the Nohkalikai Falls viewpoint, one of India's tallest plunge waterfalls.

itinerary.description:
Start early after breakfast and drive to Tyrna village, the trailhead for Nongriat.
Walk down the stone steps to the double-decker living root bridge, with time to rest and look around.
Climb back up at your own pace, accompanied by your trip captain and a local guide.
If time and weather allow, see Seven Sisters Falls and Mawsmai Cave.
Overnight stay in Cherrapunji.

itinerary.description:
After breakfast, drive towards Mawlynnong, around three hours from Cherrapunji.
Walk through the village and to the nearby living root bridge.
Continue to Dawki for a boat ride on the Umngot river, subject to water conditions.
Walk to the suspension bridge and enjoy the river view near the border.
Overnight stay in Dawki or nearby.

itinerary.title: Return to Shillong | Evening at Leisure
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, enjoy a relaxed morning by the river.
Drive back to Shillong, around three hours, with a lunch stop on the way.
Check in and spend the evening at the Police Bazaar or at leisure.
Overnight stay in Shillong.

itinerary.description:
After breakfast, check out of the hotel.
Drive to Guwahati, about three hours, for your onward flight or train.
Plan departures from the evening onwards to allow for road delays.

honeymoon_trips.title: Meghalaya Honeymoon: Misty Hills, Waterfalls and a Candlelight Dinner
honeymoon_trips.summary: Five unhurried nights for two in the Abode of Clouds, with Laitlum Canyons, Cherrapunji's waterfalls, a private boat ride on the Umngot at Dawki, a couples spa session and a candlelight dinner.
honeymoon_trips.overview:
This private honeymoon takes you through Meghalaya's hill landscapes at an easy pace: four nights in Shillong and one in Cherrapunji, travelling by private car. Mornings start late, and each day has just one or two outings.

You see Laitlum Canyons and Elephant Falls, the cliffs and waterfalls around Cherrapunji, the village of Mawlynnong and the clear Umngot river at Dawki. The root bridge walk near Mawlynnong is short and easy, while the longer Nongriat trek can be added on request.

Expect a flower welcome and bed decoration on arrival, a couples spa session and a candlelight dinner, all subject to availability. Tell us your wedding date at booking and we will pass it to the hotels.

custom_trips.summary: A private five-night circuit of Meghalaya's best-known sights, from Shillong's waterfalls and lakes to Cherrapunji, Mawlynnong and the clear Umngot at Dawki.
custom_trips.overview:
The Classic Circuit is the most popular way to see Meghalaya, with two nights in Shillong, one in Cherrapunji, one near Dawki and a final night in Shillong. You travel by private car, with time for Elephant Falls, Laitlum Canyons, Mawsmai Cave, Nohkalikai Falls and Seven Sisters Falls.

You also walk through Mawlynnong village and take a boat ride on the Umngot river at Dawki. The Nongriat root bridge trek and a Kaziranga extension can be added on request.

custom_trips.overview:

custom_trips.title: Meghalaya Adventure: Root Bridge Trek, Dawki and Kaziranga Safari
custom_trips.summary: A seven-night active route with the Nongriat root bridge trek, the Umngot river at Dawki and a Kaziranga jeep safari in Assam, travelling by private car.
custom_trips.overview:
This trip is for travellers who want a more active route. After Shillong and Laitlum Canyons you base yourself in Cherrapunji for the long trek down to the double-decker living root bridge at Nongriat. You then move to the Dawki area for the Umngot river, where optional kayaking or snorkelling may be arranged in the dry season.

The last two nights are in Kaziranga, Assam, for jeep safaris to see the one-horned rhinoceros and other wildlife. Kaziranga is usually closed in the monsoon, so this trip is best from November to March; ask us for a Meghalaya-only version if you travel at another time. The price is on request because it depends on the season and the activities you choose.
highlights: Laitlum Canyons and Shillong
Long trek to the double-decker living root bridge at Nongriat
Nohkalikai Falls near Cherrapunji
Mawlynnong village and the Umngot river at Dawki
Optional kayaking, snorkelling or camping near Dawki, in the dry season
Jeep safari at Kaziranga National Park, subject to park timings
